text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz proposes alliance with leftists and Tansu Ciller, leader of the coalition's conservative wing, to form the next government.
- The Islamist-led coalition is shaking just ahead of a critical meeting with the military as MPs from both wings of the coalition prepare to withdraw from government or resign.
- Acting commander of the army walked out of parliament when ruling Islamists and leftist opposition leader Bulent Ecevit began arguing bitterly.
- New government alternatives are already been considered in Ankara as current Islamist-led government is not expected to last for another month.
- Ciller says her party would withdraw from the government if the Islamist wing in power did not agree to eight years of uninterrupted, secularist education.
- Thirty people detained for demonstrating against a gold mine in western town of Bergama.
- International rating agency Moody's reveals a very critical report on financial situation of Turkish banks.
- Two U.S. companies send letter to President Bill Clinton asking for help in lifting "secret arms embargo" on Turkey ahead a helicopter tender.
